items.title: Rain-battered Chennai braces for more heavy showers, CM Vijay reviews preparations
items.summary: Chennai and several other districts of Tamil Nadu are likely to receive heavy rainfall on Sunday, October 18, with the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) forecasting further intense spells amid the active northeast monsoon. The forecast follows heavy rain on Saturday, October 17, when parts of Chennai recorded more than 300 mm. The downpour inundated roads, disrupted traffic and increased the combined storage of the city’s five principal drinking water reservoirs by 237 million cubic feet (mcft) over two days. On Sunday, Chief Minister Vijay inspected the Greater Chennai Corporation headquarters at Ripon Building to review preparations for the northeast monsoon and stormwater drainage measures. The RMC has forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Villupuram, Cuddalore, Salem, Krishnagiri, the Nilgiris and several other districts. The department attributed the rainfall to a cyclonic circulation over northern Tamil Nadu and adjoining southern coastal Andhra Pradesh.
